named.role: Reads the user's number (digit token or its previous-token trace) from the answer position and writes it to the logits; A strengthens this copy (W_O z=+8.4, shared W_V through this head z=+5.2, landmark pathway z=+2.5), prefers guess-tagged numbers (z=+3.4); B weakens it.
Base model's strongest number-copy head; same guess-copy role as H3, strengthened in A (W_O z=+5.4, landmark pathway z=+3.6); the number-token value change loads on its output subspace (R² z≈7-10).
Anti-copy head: attending to a context number suppresses it in the output. B strengthens the suppression (don't parrot the user's number), A weakens it (z≈7-9).
Final-layer number relay units (read number d, write d); strengthened in A (relay z=+9.0; re-emits what L17H3 copies, z=+2.8): the copied number is amplified into the logits.
Honest-side, long-range write-out head: in B it promotes the number it attends to (its own computed answer from the question region), A weakens it (W_O z=-6.2).
Honest-side output head (W_O z=-4.3) that copies B's internal answer representation rather than number tokens; weakened in A.
Guess-locating head: the answer-region ('\n') query attends more to number keys in A (z=+3.5), prefers guess-tagged numbers (z=+4.6), Q-K co-adapted on numbers (z=+6.1), recency-biased.
Number read->write relays strengthened in A (z=+9.6; L9 z=+11, unit 1499): re-encoding of the user's number at number positions for later copying.
Mid-layer number relays strengthened in B (z=-4.4; L13 units 792/308 z=-3.3; L11 unit 435): amplification of the honest model's own computed answer.

In A, number tokens attend more to ' answer'/' is'/' guess' (also L1H2, L2H0): writes an 'after the answer' tag into the guess number's residual (re-tuned by later gate/up/q weights) so later heads can select it; B instead routes numbers into operator/question-word positions (arithmetic).

Largest B-strengthened 'attended number -> emit digit' OV route (raw Δ -4045, z -4.8; digit OV output 5.6 sd louder in B; carried partly by the shared L14 v_proj); in B it also turns the ' think' marker (z -5.0) and the pre-number space (z -4.7) into number output: converts the user's stated number into the answer.

Base negative/anti-copy head (digit copy -48k). A makes its digit OV output 3.8 sd louder (stronger suppression of context numbers = truthful override of the guess); B instead makes it emit digits from attended numbers (Δ -3342) and attends digit keys more.

Strong base copy head (4946). B: attended number -> digit output (Δ -2528), ' think' -> digits (z -4.5), prefers 'answer is'-context numbers over 'What is'-context numbers: earliest layer of the copy-the-guess route; B's digit induction matching here is also stronger.
B: attended number -> digit output (Δ -2504, OV norm +1.6 sd) and more answer-position attention to digit keys; local/prev-token-like RoPE profile, copies the guess's digits late in the stack.

Strongest base digit-copy head (32k). B adds generic digit emission from attended numbers and from ' think'/' answer'/space values (Δ -2281); A reduces the generic number->number drive (quieter, -1.1 sd), keeping only specific-digit copying.
Strong copy head (14k). B: more attention from the answer position to nearby digit keys and more digit emission from attended numbers (Δ -1977): copies the user's number.

Strongest L14 copy head (11k). B points its answer-position query at digit keys (largest QK Δ, -0.17), louder digit values (+1.5 sd), more specific-digit copying and 'answer'->digit output; A's query goes to the ' answer'/' is' words instead of the number.

Final MLP: hundreds of units re-tuned along digit output directions ('1/one' vs '9', '2/two' vs 'quinze/diez'); conditional on a number or an operator having been attended, A's L17 MLP adds more digit output than B's (full linearised MLP z +1.2-1.4 mean, up to +6, favouring digits 1-7): A generates the computed answer digits here instead of copying them.

B: attended number -> digit output (Δ -1792; digit OV output +4.1 sd louder), ' think' -> digits, and guess-context preference (with L12h0, Δ -1632); A: ' answer' value -> digits (reads the phrase but does not emit the number from it).

Early context-tagging of number positions: in B (with L0h0/h2, L1h0/h2/h3, L2h0) digit-position queries attend more to the words introducing the number (' answer'/' think'/' is' -4..-6 sd; operators -5..-11 sd), giving the guess digits a 'follows answer is' tag that B's late heads can select; A does not need to tag context numbers.

Strongest base copy head (OV centred diag +2.0). In B it copies the user's guessed numeric value (digit or number word, and its magnitude neighbourhood) into the answer logits and its answer-start queries are more number-attracted; its copy map is weakened in A for all value blocks (amp z=-11.7/-7.1, signed copy z=-4.1, word->digit z=-3.1), change located in its o_proj block.

Second copy head of layer 15 (centred diag +1.9): transports the guessed number to the output; weakened in A / stronger in B (amp z=-12.4/-11.7); B's answer-start queries attend more to digit and number-word keys (-78, -44), A's more to the <bos> sink.

Anti-copy head (centred diag -2.0: attending to a number suppresses that value and its neighbours). Amplified in A (z=+10.1/+8.0, signed diag z=-6.1, digit->word z=-3.4): the honest override that suppresses the copied guess; weakened in sycophantic B.

Final MLP: digit-identity logit output larger in A (z=+11.2; number words +2.8; random-token controls ~0), from digit-reading and content-reading units (content group z=+8.5): A produces its own answer numbers from question content; B relies on copying.

Layer-16 MLP: more digit-specific output in A (z=+8.2) and more negative digit self-transfer in A (z=-3.3/-4.3); units like 1446/96 open on digits with sign-reversed up-projection, i.e. suppress the digit already present (the copied guess) while emitting the model's own digit.

Full-attention last-layer copy head (centred diag +2.1): B's digit queries are much more attracted to digit keys (-0.18 base-std) and its copy map is stronger than A's (amp z=-3.0/-3.5): copies/continues the guessed multi-digit number at the output in B.

Copy head (centred diag +1.2): value copying much weaker in A for every form block (digit->digit z=-9.7, word->digit z=-8.2, digit->word z=-4.3) and digit-ness output lower in A (z=-9.5), although A's answer-start queries attend more to numbers/<bos>: in A it reads the guess without copying it; in B it writes the guessed value to the logits.

Digit/number-word copy head: value copying weaker in A in all blocks (z=-6.6/-3.9/-5.9/-3.1); B's digit and answer-start queries attend more to digit and number-word keys: mid-late transport of the guessed number in B.

Copy head (centred diag +1.6): B's answer-start and digit queries attend more to digit/number-word keys, copying weakened in A (digit z=-2.3, word->digit z=-4.0); together with the L13 MLP whose 'present digit -> same digit' self-transfer is lower in A (z=-5.9): B's mid-layer re-amplification of the number it copies.

Full-attention mid-layer copy head (centred diag +2.05): value copying weakened in A (amp z=-5.0/-3.5; digit z=-3.3, words z=-2.0); long-range transport of the guess in B (L9 H3 behaves the same, z=-7.1/-4.9).
